commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Match duplicate handling to the app
commitResults.messageBody:
UC02 lets the recruiter proceed after a duplicate email or phone
number is detected, and a user story promises a warning for such
matches. The app rejects exact duplicates outright, with no override,
and only warns when a phone number may be another candidate's number
written differently, such as with or without +65.

Let's update UC02 so an exact duplicate ends the use case without
adding the candidate, and add an extension for the possible-match
warning. Let's also narrow the user story to that warning, since the
existing "be stopped from adding" story covers exact duplicates.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Generalise phone-match user story benefit
commitResults.messageBody:
The user story for the possible phone-match warning gives "with or
without a country code" as its benefit. That ties the story to one
way of writing the same number, which is an implementation detail
rather than the user's goal.

Let's describe the benefit as catching a candidate entered twice with
a differently formatted number, which covers every case the warning
handles.

The phone-match user story's benefit restates its want, and its want
mentions only new candidates although editing a phone number also
triggers the warning. The story also reads much like the must-have
story for blocking duplicates, without saying why this one only warns.

Let's say "a candidate's phone number" so edits are covered, and give
the benefit as spotting a likely duplicate without blocking different
people whose numbers only look alike. This matches the design choice
of warning rather than rejecting a possible match.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Define core terms in glossary
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG uses "pending", "final outcome" and "experience level"
throughout, but the glossary does not define them. It does define
"candidate status history" and "command shortcut", which belong to
features that are not implemented, so readers may assume those exist.

Let's add the three missing terms, listing the statuses each status
term covers. Let's keep the two planned terms, since the optional use
cases UC22 and UC25 still use them, but mark them as not yet
implemented and point to those use cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Name role status values in glossary
commitResults.messageBody:
The glossary defines role status only as "the recorded state of
recruitment", though the requirements refer to open and closed roles
throughout and a closed role accepts no new candidates. Readers cannot
tell from the glossary what states a role can be in.

Let's name the OPEN and CLOSED values in the existing entry and state
what closing a role means for its candidates, rather than adding
separate entries for each value.

The role opening entry says the vacancy is "tracked in RecruiterBuddy",
which the whole DG already implies, and explains that "role" means a
job position rather than that it is short for role opening. The role
status entry repeats the contrast with candidate progress that the
candidate status entry already makes.

Let's shorten the role opening entry and state that it is also called
a role, and drop the repeated contrast from the role status entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Nest use-case groups under Use cases
commitResults.messageBody:
The "Must-have" and "Optional" group headings are level 2, although
they sit inside the level-3 "Use cases" section. The page navigation
lists them beside the Appendix sections, so they look like top-level
parts of the DG rather than groups of use cases.

Let's make the group headings level 4 and each use case level 5, so
the groups nest under "Use cases" and each use case nests under its
group.

The NFRs run 1 to 6, then 3, 4 and 8 onwards, so 3 and 4 appear twice
and 7 is missing. Readers cannot refer to a requirement by number
without ambiguity.

Let's number the NFRs 1 to 17 in order. No other part of the docs
refers to an NFR by number, so nothing else needs updating.

commitResults.messageTitle: InterviewCommand: Use singular "other" for one unnamed clash
commitResults.messageBody:
The same-time warning names up to two clashing candidates and counts
the rest as "(+N others)". With exactly one candidate left over, it
reads "(+1 others)", which is ungrammatical and was reported during
testing.

Let's use "other" when one candidate is left over and "others" for
more, keeping the existing wording otherwise. Update the test that
expected "(+1 others)", and add a test with four clashing candidates
to cover the plural case.

The acknowledgement lists only the add, note and interview commands,
sample data and diagrams. Claude Code also assisted with the duplicate
and contact warnings in edit, the note and interview display on
candidate cards, command warning messages, and User Guide and
Developer Guide updates, so the declaration under-reports its use.

Let's name these contributions too, and drop the repeated "and" in
the list, so readers can see which work was AI-assisted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Messages: Leave out empty note, interview and tags
commitResults.messageBody:
The add, edit and delete success messages print every candidate field,
so a candidate without a note, interview or tags shows
"Note: ; Interview: ; Tags: " with blank values. This was reported
during testing and differs from the candidate card, which hides an
empty note or interview.

Let's include these three optional fields in Messages.format(Person)
only when they have a value, so all three commands show a cleaner
message. Add MessagesTest, since the method had no direct test, with
one case without optional fields and one with all of them.
Update acknowledgement

commitResults.messageTitle: Messages: Keep tags in candidate summary
commitResults.messageBody:
Leaving out empty tags changes how every candidate without tags is
summarized, which goes beyond the reported note and interview problem.

Let's restore the original tags output and limit this fix to the note
and interview, updating MessagesTest to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Note that phone brackets and extensions are rejected
commitResults.messageBody:
The PHONE_NUMBER rules say which characters a phone number may have,
but not that common notations such as "(65) 9123 4568" or
"9123 4569 ext 12" are rejected. Testers expected these to work.

Accepting them would change phone validation, duplicate checks and
storage during the feature freeze. Let's state the limit in the UG
instead, showing how to write a country code with + and suggesting
the candidate's note for an extension.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Split phone symbol advice into sub-bullets
commitResults.messageBody:
The phone advice joins two unrelated tips in one sentence and gives
"note 1 Phone ext 12" as an example, which reads like part of a phone
number rather than a separate command. It also does not warn that a
new note replaces the existing one.

Let's give the country code and extension tips their own sub-bullets,
link to the note command instead of showing its syntax, and mention
that a new note replaces the old one.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Describe Singapore phone check as a reminder
commitResults.messageBody:
The PHONE_NUMBER rules say a number without a country code "is treated
as a Singapore number", which suggests the app assumes or changes
something about it. The app only compares the number with the
Singapore format to decide whether to add a warning, and saves it
unchanged either way.

Let's describe it as a check against the Singapore format, with a
reminder to add the country code if the number is overseas.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Move phone symbol limits after separator rule
commitResults.messageBody:
The bullet on rejected phone symbols sits between "can include spaces
and hyphens" and the Singapore format check, splitting the rules about
which characters a number may contain.

Let's place it after the bullet on how spaces and hyphens are saved,
so the character rules read together and the Singapore check comes
first.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Explain the + in phone numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
The PHONE_NUMBER rules allow an optional + at the start but do not say
what it is for, although later bullets refer to the country code.

Let's say that the + introduces a country code, so the later bullets
on country codes read clearly.

commitResults.messageTitle: MessagesTest: Rename test for note and interview
commitResults.messageBody:
The test name format_noteAndInterview_includesEachOnce suggests it
checks for duplicate labels, but it checks that both the note and the
interview appear in the message.

Rename it to format_noteAndInterview_includesBoth to match what it
checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify delete errors for extra arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
Delete parses the entire argument string as an index, so extra text
makes a valid index appear invalid.

Validate the index separately and reject trailing arguments with a
specific message. Preserve genuine index errors and reject the whole
command before execution so no candidate is deleted accidentally.
